plan: Since this functions as a second-price auction (I pay the clock price when others exit, not my own bid), bidding my true value of $49 is the dominant strategy. This ensures I win whenever profitable (my value exceeds the second-highest bid) and never overpay, since I'd only pay what others bid, which will be at most $49. Bidding below true value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above is unnecessary since I have the maximum possible value.

Since this functions as a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, if I win), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding higher risks overpaying beyond my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Bidding exactly $44 maximizes expected profit by ensuring I win whenever the price is below my value and never pay more than my value.

Since the sealed bid acts as my exit price in an ascending clock auction with 2 other bidders (effectively second-price mechanics), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding above value risks paying more than the item is worth to me; bidding below reduces my chance of winning profitable auctions. Bidding exactly $22 ensures I win whenever the clock price would leave me profit (price < value) and I never pay more than my value.
